property_summary: After making a Deposit of value v (>= MinDeposit) the caller's recorded balance is at least v and never less than the freshly deposited amount.

For any caller and deposit amount >= MinDeposit, the reference contract never overflows so balances[caller] after Deposit equals old + msg.value (i.e., balances increases monotonically by msg.value); removing the overflow check allows an overflow that makes balances differ (wrap-around) for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposit amount >= MinDeposit, the correct contract ensures balances[caller] after Deposit equals previous balances[caller] + msg.value (no wrap-around), whereas the mutant (without the require overflow check) can overflow and make balances differ for some inputs.

For any caller and deposit amount >= MinDeposit that we allow (bounded to be <= type(uint).max - balances[caller]), the reference C guarantees balances[caller] after Deposit equals previous balances[caller] + msg.value (no wrap-around); removing the require allows an overflow/wrap-around for some large msg.value, which the mutant can trigger and thus violates this invariant.

For any depositor and deposit amount >= MinDeposit, the reference contract ensures balances[depositor] after Deposit is >= previous balances[depositor] (no wrap-around), while removing the require allows arithmetic wrap-around causing balances to become smaller than before for some inputs.

For any depositor and any deposit value >= MinDeposit, the reference contract guarantees that no balance wrap-around occurs so that there exists no address k whose balances increases by an amount that is inconsistent with safe addition (i.e., balances[k] after Deposit is either unchanged for k!=depositor or equals previous + msg.value for k==depositor); the mutant removing the require can overflow and make balances differ (wrap) for some inputs.
